paper_title: Protect the Parent, Spare the Child: Protecting Prefixes in RPKI before All Origins Are Known

title_contract.parent: the aggregate prefix p_0, whose origin a_h is already known and explicitly named
title_contract.child: a proper subprefix p contained by p_0, whose future origin may not yet be enumerable when policy is installed
title_contract.all_origins: the complete set of future proper-subprefix origins; the aggregate origin is not unknown
title_contract.protecting_prefixes: preserve explicit protection of the known-origin aggregate while bounding signed proper-subprefix scope
title_contract.boundary: OpenScope exposes weaker open-scope provenance. It neither authenticates nor conventionally authorizes an unlisted origin

paper_argument: Subprefix-Scope ROV (S²-ROV) protects a known-origin aggregate before every future proper-subprefix origin can be enumerated, while giving scope-matched routes an independent OpenScope signal for local routing policy.
contributions: C1: We formalize the aggregate-subprefix dilemma as a validation and origin-visibility problem and prove the aggregate-coverage and indistinguishable-origin limits.

C2: We design a deterministic four-state S²-ROV classifier whose OpenScope state separates holder-signed prefix and length limits from explicit origin authorization, making it strictly more expressive for the aggregate-subprefix dilemma.

C3: We identify 587 RIPE/RRC00 candidate paths across 97 roots, implement a dual-stack prototype, and evaluate conflicts during partial ROA issuance, policy prioritization, processing cost, intended-route delivery, and unlisted-origin exposure. At 50% ROA issuance, configuring S²-ROV policies for 80% of aggregate prefixes reduces both mean conflict rates by 79.1%.

notation.o: origin AS observed in the BGP route
notation.a: origin AS explicitly authorized by a modeled ROA
notation.a_h: aggregate-origin AS named by an issuer authorized for p_0 under RPKI, not the holder identifier
notation.v: policy-profile version binding structural and ASN-eligibility rules
notation.w_v: address width selected by profile version v: 32 for IPv4 and 128 for IPv6

datasets.name: RIPE/RIS visibility-path characterization
datasets.description: Status-specific IPv4 and IPv6 allocation paths from the RIPE Database, joined to exact-prefix origin sets from one RIPE RIS RRC00 RIB. Table I reports RIPE Database, BGP Data, and Origin Divergence observations by the number d of recorded intermediate allocations.

datasets.name: Partial S²-ROV deployment replay
datasets.description: The 504 IPv4 and 83 IPv6 origin-divergence candidates from Table I are pooled into 587 endpoint-prefix bundles and expanded into 589 observed route-origin outcomes under 97 IP-version-qualified roots. All endpoint routes are announced. Figure 2 reports means over 1,000 fixed-seed randomized deployment replays, using independent nested orders for downstream exact ROAs, root ROAs, and aggregate prefixes configured with S²-ROV policies. It varies the ROA issuance target from 0% to 100% and compares S²-ROV policy shares of 0%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100%. Figure 3 fixes issuance at 50% and compares Route count, ASRank, AS degree, and Random prioritization.

datasets.name: Semantic-conformance corpus
datasets.description: Frozen IPv4 correctness gate comprising 106,218 legal route-policy vectors, 100,000 malformed trials, 58 fixed parser mutations, 306,967 rule-order checks, and 264,532 projected ROA entries. Separate dual-stack checks cover boundary prefixes, encoding, and mixed-family rejection.

datasets.name: Construction stress corpus
datasets.description: A separate IPv4 workload containing 8,830 leaves under 1,647 roots, used for policy construction, canonical round trips, and bounded ancestor-probe checks.

datasets.name: Selected fixture testbed
datasets.description: A controlled Krill 0.14.4, Routinator 0.13.2, and FRR 10.6.1 path with one selected local fixture as the sole S²-ROV policy input and an ordinary RTR view as the conventional ROV baseline.

datasets.name: Controlled selected-policy replay
datasets.description: Matched single-core IPv4 and IPv6 replays derived from the 24 June 2026 RRC00 RIB. Within each IP version, one fixed 4,096-route query set is repeated 32 times against policies containing 1, 64, 256, 1,024, and 4,096 total records. Active Figure 4(a) reports arithmetic-mean fixed-output classification throughput; the run's policy-load measurements remain historical and non-plotted.

datasets.name: Same-size policy update benchmark
datasets.description: A matched single-core IPv4 and IPv6 benchmark adds the OpenScope marker to the base entry of an otherwise identical active policy at 1, 64, 256, 1,024, and 4,096 total records. Each of ten cells uses 20 fresh processes. Figure 4(b) reports arithmetic-mean deserialization, active-policy replacement, and first-classification latency.

datasets.name: Fixed-scenario routing model
datasets.description: The frozen 36,800-scenario Phase 7 campaign is preserved. A separately hash-bound 14,000-scenario extension fills the seven missing decile points, yielding 11 coverage points from 0% to 100% of one opaque fixed 589-AS scenario set over the same 200 selected units and five fixed random orders. A separate 210-scenario IPv6 sensitivity covers 21 origin pairs under eight roots. Intended-only and origin-competition announcement sets separately quantify delivery benefit and unlisted-origin exposure on the family-neutral graph.

baselines.name: Separately implemented specification oracle

baselines.name: Conventional ROV view

baselines.name: Endpoint-specific exact placement
baselines.description: At each q target, the s=0 condition supplies the aggregate-plus-matching-ROA baseline for the Invalid-route comparison.

baselines.name: Announcement-matched aggregate-only ROV

metrics.name: semantic conformance failures

metrics.name: route-state and action agreement

metrics.name: secondary equal-decision coverage
metrics.description: Auxiliary share of the frozen IPv4 or IPv6 candidates addressed by equal numbers of endpoint-specific or root-scope decisions. This is retained as a secondary artifact, not as Figure 2 or a headline result.

metrics.name: replayed Invalid-route rate
metrics.description: Mean share of the fixed 589 endpoint route-origin pairs classified Invalid at each downstream-ROA issuance level and each share of aggregate prefixes with an S²-ROV policy.

metrics.name: placement-sensitive Invalid-route rate
metrics.description: Mean share of the fixed 589 endpoint route-origin pairs classified Invalid at 50% downstream ROA issuance as aggregate prefixes are configured with S²-ROV in each prioritization order.

metrics.name: selected-policy classification cost
metrics.description: Arithmetic-mean single-core fixed-output classification throughput for controlled policies containing 1, 64, 256, 1,024, and 4,096 total records. Historical policy-load measurements are retained but not plotted.

metrics.name: same-size policy update latency
metrics.description: Arithmetic-mean local policy-replacement latency at 1, 64, 256, 1,024, and 4,096 total records. Timing includes deserialization of the updated in-memory payload, active-policy replacement, and the fixed route's first OpenScope classification.

metrics.name: intended-route delivery
metrics.description: Absolute destination-delivery percentage under S²-ROV, Aggregate-only ROV, and Exact-match ROV in the intended-only routing-model announcement set. OpenScope remains the S²-ROV route-classification state; the latter two labels denote conventional ROV under the stated ROA configurations.

metrics.name: unlisted-origin delivery
metrics.description: Absolute destination-delivery percentage to the eligible unlisted origin under S²-ROV, Aggregate-only ROV, and Exact-match ROV in the separate competition announcement set. OpenScope remains the S²-ROV route-classification state; the latter two labels denote conventional ROV under the stated ROA configurations.

S²-ROV preserves the aggregate's Explicit state and provides OpenScope as an independent local-policy signal

background.title: Aggregate--Subprefix Authorization Gap
key_arguments: Formal ROV matching semantics
A proof that keeping an aggregate Valid necessarily makes an unmatched different-origin proper subprefix Invalid
A formal origin-choice visibility proposition showing why an issuer that cannot distinguish two downstream choices cannot guarantee an exact origin listing for both
A status-specific dual-stack characterization of RIPE Database paths, BGP Data, and Origin Divergence using RIPE RIS RRC00
Two requirements derived from Propositions 1 and 2: bounded descendant scope and provenance separation

key_points: ROA prefix entry (q,a,ell)
ROA cover and match
RFC 6811/8481 states
a Valid aggregate guarantees that some ROA covers every proper subprefix
a different-origin proper subprefix is Invalid until a matching ROA becomes available
the result holds for any maxLength because coverage is independent of the match conditions

paragraph_outline.topic: II-A closing: ROV consequence and the missing-ROA premise
key_points: changing maxLength cannot authorize a different origin
withholding the aggregate ROA avoids the conflict only by removing aggregate protection

conclusion.title: Conclusion
key_arguments: Propositions 1 and 2 establish the aggregate-subprefix validation and origin-visibility limits
Proposition 3 establishes a state separation that conventional ROV cannot represent
At 50% ROA issuance, configuring S²-ROV policies for 80% of aggregate prefixes lowers the mean potential conflict rate from 50.1% to 10.5% and the mean observed conflict rate from 24.8% to 5.2%
The dual-stack prototype and fixed routing analyses quantify processing cost, intended-route delivery, and unlisted-origin exposure
Exact ROAs provide origin-specific validation once the origin is known, while S²-ROV records holder-signed prefix and length limits until then

key_points: two requirements and four-state semantics
at the 50% issuance target, configuring S²-ROV policies for 80% of aggregate prefixes lowers the mean potential conflict rate from 50.1% to 10.5% and the observed conflict rate from 24.8% to 5.2%
the dual-stack replay quantifies classification throughput and same-size policy-update latency

at full deployment within the fixed routing model, intended delivery is 99.2% under S²-ROV versus 82.1% under Aggregate-only ROV and equals the 99.2% Exact-match ROV reference; in a separate competition set, unlisted-origin delivery is 41.2%, 32.4%, and 11.7% under the same three configurations, respectively
complete objects, multi-object composition, lifecycle handling, and native enforcement remain open
